info.name: DigUp Search
info.summary: Semantic media search from a self-hosted DigUp server: photos, video frames and sound, audio, PDFs and documents — filtered to the files each user can see.
info.description:
DigUp Search connects a Nextcloud instance to a self-hosted DigUp server (https://github.com/ARahim3/DigUp), a semantic media search engine that indexes a folder tree read-only — photos, video frames *and their sound*, audio, PDFs, office documents, screenshots — and answers natural-language queries with z-scored hits.
* **The operator pastes the server URL and its read token** in Administration settings → DigUp Search. The server may live on another machine (the one with the GPU); Nextcloud talks to it server-to-server. * **Per-user by design**: every search is filtered inside Nextcloud against its own permissions — a user sees their own files plus files shared with them, and nothing else. The DigUp server's index spans the whole data directory; the filtering happens here, with Nextcloud's own APIs. * **Read-only, by design**: the app never writes files and never touches Nextcloud's database beyond its own settings. It creates no tables. Media bytes reach the browser from Nextcloud's own preview API, with the user's own session — the DigUp token never leaves the server. * Open a result: the Files app opens it (viewer for images, Videos for video, PDF viewer for PDFs). * The server side (compose shape, tokens, exclusions, the ACL contract) is documented in the DigUp repository: docs/implementation/stage-12-integrations.md.
info.author: Dean Swilling
